findings.claim: In TopicEmbed.import, the 'Imported from' footer interpolates url unescaped into a single-quoted <a href='#{url}'> in raw HTML. Because the post uses cook_method raw_html, the sanitizer never runs, so a crafted embed_url allows HTML/JS injection (stored XSS).

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into `#{url}`, guarded only by `=~ /^https?:\/\//` (line 11), and the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html` (line 22), which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` unsanitised (app/models/post.rb:133). `embed_url` comes straight from `params` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9,15) and `URI()` accepts single quotes, so a URL like `http://host/?a='onmouseover='alert(1)` injects an event-handler attribute; `<`/`>` are rejected by `URI()`, so it is attribute injection rather than tag injection, and not executed here.

findings.claim: The raw_html cook method returns raw unchanged and skips sanitization. Remote content is stored as cooked HTML verbatim: RSS HTML that is only CGI.unescapeHTML'd, and Readability output that keeps javascript: hrefs. Later edits of such posts are also cooked raw.

verifier.reason: app/models/post.rb:133 returns `raw` unsanitised for raw_html posts, and the before_save at app/models/post.rb:321 re-cooks the same way on every later edit. app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 only applies CGI.unescapeHTML, and app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 and :48-52 store that content with no protocol filtering (Readability whitelists tags and href/src only; the gem source is not in the repo, so the javascript: href detail rests on its known behaviour); it is then rendered unescaped at app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19.

findings.claim: embed/best.html.erb uses '<%- end if %>' instead of '<%- end %>'. The stray postfix 'if' makes the block's closing conditional on the next buffer append, or is invalid syntax.

verifier.reason: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 (new file in the patch) closes the header if/else with `<%- end if %>`, where line 22 uses a plain `<%- end %>`. Not executed, but with the locked erubis 2.7.0 this should compile to `end if ;`, a Ruby syntax error that fails every render of the embed view; spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb has no `render_views`, so the specs would not catch it.

findings.claim: The embed iframe passes request.referer, a full URL, as postMessage's targetOrigin instead of an origin (scheme://host[:port]). The parent page therefore does not receive the resize messages.

verifier.reason: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 does pass the full `request.referer` URL as targetOrigin, but the HTML spec has postMessage parse targetOrigin as a URL and compare only its origin, so the path is ignored. The message is still delivered to the parent listener at app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15-25, so the claimed failure does not occur.

findings.claim: The parent page's postMessage origin check uses substring matching (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of strict origin comparison. Origins that are substrings or prefixes of discourseUrl pass validation.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 validates the sender with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring test, so any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. `http://discourse.example.co` against `http://discourse.example.com/`) passes. The only effect of a forged message is setting the iframe height at embed.js:20-21.

findings.claim: The postMessage height value is used without being parsed or validated.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:20-21 only truthiness-checks `e.data.height` and then assigns `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` with no parseInt, type check or range check. The only guard is the loose substring origin test at embed.js:17, and the value goes into a DOM property, so the worst case is a wrong iframe height, not injection.

findings.claim: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value and only works because browsers ignore invalid values.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL" (asserted in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:37); ALLOWALL is not a defined value (only DENY, SAMEORIGIN and the obsolete ALLOW-FROM are), so framing is permitted only because browsers ignore the unrecognised value. It is a common Rails idiom and behaves as intended in practice.

findings.claim: Setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL disables clickjacking protection. The referer check relies on a spoofable header, and it falls back to an empty string when the referer is nil.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 sets X-Frame-Options to "ALLOWALL", gated only by the Referer-host comparison at line 26 (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which a non-browser client can forge. The empty-string fallback is real but harmless: `URI('').host` is nil, so a missing referer is rejected, and the header is limited to the read-only embed endpoint.

findings.claim: request.referer is written into a JavaScript string in the embed layout without JS-context escaping.

verifier.reason: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 interpolates `'<%= request.referer %>'` inside a `<script>` string with only ERB's default HTML escaping, no `escape_javascript`/`to_json`. Exploitability is limited: HTML escaping still neutralises quotes and `</script>`, and app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 requires the referer host to equal `embeddable_host`.

findings.claim: The migration adds a column to posts with default: 1, null: false in a single step. On PostgreSQL < 11 this rewrites the table under an exclusive lock, which takes a long time on large tables.

verifier.reason: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` in one step; on PostgreSQL before 11 (the only versions available for this 2013-era codebase) ADD COLUMN with a non-null default rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.

findings.claim: The patch edits an already-shipped top_topics create_table migration to add force: true. This has no effect where the migration already ran, and drops an existing top_topics table on a fresh run.

verifier.reason: The patch changes the pre-existing migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 from `create_table :top_topics do` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do`. Rails skips migrations already recorded in schema_migrations, so the edit does nothing there, and wherever the migration does run `force: true` drops any existing top_topics table before recreating it.

findings.claim: The create_topic_embeds migration uses force: true, which drops an existing topic_embeds table and its data.

verifier.reason: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 calls `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails drops any existing table of that name before creating it. No earlier migration creates topic_embeds and the same `force: true` idiom is used across the repo (e.g. db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3), so real data loss is unlikely in a normal migration run.

findings.claim: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x.png) as root-relative because they start with '/'. It rewrites them to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png in both the a[href] and img[src] loops.

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-65 and :70-71 match any value starting with '/' and strip all leading slashes via sub(/^\/+/, ''), so //cdn.example.com/x.png becomes "#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x.png" (e.g. http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png) in both the a[href] and img[src] loops; there is no guard for protocol-relative URLs.

findings.claim: absolutize_urls duplicates the a[href]/img[src] rewriting loop.

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:62-67 and 68-73 are two structurally identical loops (one for `a`/`href`, one for `img`/`src`) differing only in tag and attribute name; the file is newly added by the patch. This is copy-paste duplication only, with no behavioural defect.

findings.claim: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in PollFeed fetches an unvalidated URL. This allows SSRF to internal services, file:// URLs, or cloud metadata endpoints.

verifier.reason: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url straight to Kernel#open (open-uri loaded at line 7) with no scheme or host check, and config/site_settings.yml:356 declares it as a plain string with no validator, so internal and metadata HTTP endpoints, local paths and even "|cmd" pipes are reachable. The value is settable only by an admin, and literal file:// URLs are not actually handled by open-uri, so the claim overstates that detail.

findings.claim: Kernel#open is used on URLs, so a value starting with '|' executes a shell command on the server.

verifier.reason: Kernel#open is called on a URL string at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, an unvalidated setting from config/site_settings.yml:356) and app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 (`open(url).read`, before the https? check in `import`), so a value like `|cmd` spawns a subprocess. The anonymous embed_url path is blocked by the host check at lib/topic_retriever.rb:15, so it is reachable only through the admin setting or a link in a Disqus export (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148).

findings.claim: import_remote fetches the URL without validating its format or scheme first.

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 calls `open(url).read` with no check inside `import_remote`; the only scheme check (`url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) is in `import` at app/models/topic_embed.rb:11, which runs after the fetch. The web path is partly guarded by the host comparison at lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 (host only, not scheme), while lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 passes `t[:link]` from the import file with no validation at all.

findings.claim: import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, so it can hang indefinitely.

verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 calls `open(url).read` with no timeout options or `Timeout` wrapper, on a URL that reaches it from the embed path (lib/topic_retriever.rb:52). Only Net::HTTP's default per-read timeout applies, so there is no bound on total time and a slow-dripping host can stall the worker; "indefinitely" is slightly overstated for a fully silent host.

findings.claim: PollFeed calls i.content.scrub, but RSS 2.0 items with only <description> have nil content (SimpleRSS exposes content:encoded as content_encoded). This raises NoMethodError, and with retry: false and no per-item rescue it aborts the whole feed poll.

verifier.reason: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 calls `i.content.scrub` with no nil guard or rescue inside the `rss.items.each` loop (lines 31-37), and line 12 sets `retry: false`, so a nil `content` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll. verifier.reason: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 does `contents << "\n<hr>..."` on the `contents` parameter of `TopicEmbed.import`, and `String#<<` appends in place, so the caller's string object is modified (and a frozen string would raise). findings.claim: The throttle calls setnx and then expire as two separate calls. A failure between them leaves a key with no TTL, so retrieval of that URL is blocked permanently.

Only staff (`no_throttle`, app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17) bypass it, so "permanently" holds for ordinary users until the key is deleted by hand.

findings.claim: Each anonymous request with a distinct embed_url on an embeddable host enqueues RetrieveTopic. That job runs a full synchronous PollFeed#execute and can create a new topic. The throttle is keyed per exact URL, so outbound fetches and feed processing are unbounded.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 enqueues retrieve_topic for any unknown embed_url with no login or rate limit, gated only by a spoofable Referer check (line 26). lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 keys the 60s throttle on the exact URL, so each distinct URL on the embeddable host (e.g. a varied query string) runs a synchronous Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute (line 41) plus an outbound fetch and topic creation via TopicEmbed.import_remote (line 52).
